title: Authored-edit Todo app (local, build-only, no hot reload) (extended)
description: One person building a Todo app in WinUI 3 the way people actually build one: a page, some
navigation, a grid, a handler, a view model, a bound list, then some restructuring.
Every action is exactly ONE authored edit followed by ONE save. Nothing here uses hot reload;
the baseline being measured is the plain edit -> save -> build loop.
Some saves are deliberately invalid, because that is what half-finished authoring looks like.

dimensions.title: Wiring a Click handler
description: handler-first: write the C# method, then point the XAML at it. Every save stays buildable.
xaml-first: type Click="AddButton_Click" first, then go write the method. The first save
does not build, because the generated connector calls a method that does not exist yet.

dimensions.title: Wiring an x:Bind to a view-model property
description: vm-property-first: add the property to the view model, then bind to it. Every save builds.
binding-first: write the x:Bind first, then add the property. The first save fails in the
XAML compiler, because the binding path cannot be resolved on the source type.

variants.summary: Handler before XAML, view-model property before binding. Never saves a broken wiring.
XAML before handler, binding before property. Passes through an invalid save each time.
Handler before XAML, but binding before property.
XAML before handler, but view-model property before binding.

actions.title: Add a summary TextBlock bound with x:Bind
actions.intent: Wraps the header in a StackPanel so a second line fits in row 0.
actions.note: When this lands first the XAML compiler cannot resolve Summary on TodoListViewModel. On WindowsAppSDK 2.3.x the markup compiler often fails to load its own error-string resources and reports the unresolved binding path as WMC9999 'Xaml Internal Error' with no mention of Summary at all, so both codes are accepted.

checkpoint.runtimeState: A secondary line under the header reads "1 of 2 done". It does not update yet when a todo is checked, because nothing raises the change.

actions.title: Put a two-way bound CheckBox in the item template
actions.intent: Completion has to be editable from the row. The AutomationId is bound to Title so a UI harness can address an individual row's checkbox, which is the only way to prove the two-way write-back rather than assume it.

actions.title: Raise Summary when the collection changes
actions.intent: The bound summary was static until now.

actions.title: Add the Clear done button to the input row
actions.intent: Now the markup can safely reference the handler.

checkpoint.runtimeState: Both rows carry a checkbox, and "Ship the benchmark" is already checked because it was seeded IsDone. Checking "Buy milk" as well and then clicking Clear done empties the list entirely and the summary re-reads "0 of 0 done". The list going to ZERO rather than one is the whole assertion: it is only possible if toggling the checkbox wrote IsDone back onto the TodoItem through the two-way binding.

uiChecks.note: the row CheckBox, addressed by the AutomationId bound to Title
read back before clearing, so a failure to toggle is distinguishable from a failure to clear
1 here would mean the two-way write-back did not happen
